correctness.rationale: The proof separates weak contractibility from finite-space contractibility. The order complex is exactly the vertex antistar in the barycentric subdivision of a simplex-boundary sphere, hence a ball. At atom and coatom ranks explicit order-preserving retractions are pointwise comparable with the identity and retract onto a poset with a maximum or minimum. At every internal rank, every possible point has either an empty strict side or at least two incomparable surviving immediate neighbors on each relevant side, so no beat point exists. Stong core theory then excludes contractibility. The verifier independently stress-tests every rank for k=4 through 8; those computations are not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The family is canonical rather than an arbitrary finite slice: it is obtained by deleting one face from the face poset of a simplex boundary. The result identifies an exact structural threshold by face rank and exhibits an infinite family in which the order complex is a ball while the finite space is already a core. This directly sharpens understanding of the gap between weak contractibility and contractibility in finite-space topology.
